provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program finds each 4-connected single-colour object that is not background. It converts an object when all of these hold: it has 8 cells, its bounding box is 3x3, and its centre cell is background. That is exactly a hollow 3x3 ring. The converted box is cleared to background, and then a plus sign is drawn in palette[2]: the middle row and middle column of the box. Every other object stays as it is. The hollow square and the plus are both unchanged by every rotation and reflection, so d4 needs no axis or direction change. Box detection and drawing work directly on the visible grid coordinates. Only colour roles are specialised: background = palette[0], object colour = palette[1] (all generator sprites use it), and output colour = palette[2]. Background is taken from the palette constant rather than from a most-common-colour count, so dense scenes cannot be misread.
draft_notes.limitations: This relies on the constructor's domain. Sprites never touch each other edge-to-edge, so an 8-cell component with a 3x3 box and a background centre can only come from a box sprite. If a box ever merged with another sprite, it would no longer be an isolated 8-cell 3x3 component and would not be converted. The archived solver behaves the same way. The demonstrations are not used, because the colour roles come from the palette. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule. This factory has not been run or tested by me.
